subject: Careers
title: Careers can change
weekly_outcome: Students understand that career journeys are not always straight and that people may change jobs or retrain.
weekly_outcome_verbatim: Students understand that career journeys are not always straight and that people may change jobs or retrain.
objective: I can put a simple career story in order and identify where someone adapted to change.
objective_verbatim: I can put a simple career story in order and identify where someone adapted to change.
display_objective: I can put a simple career story in order and identify where someone adapted to change.
calendar_note: Year A. Spring 1 Week 1, 4–8 January 2027. Tuesday 5 January 2027, P3. One 40-minute formative lesson for up to five learners. Spring 1 runs 4 January–12 February, six weeks; Week 6 is assessing. Source Week 5 retains its mixed evidence role. No clock time supplied.
source_adaptation: Exact E16 weekly outcome, F16 focus, G16 lesson outcome and J16 evidence retained. H16 sequence and I16 timing retained. Review is private rather than a compulsory whole-class response. K16 reduced choices, pictures, model and usual access are built in; all sources are in the pack, so no website navigation is needed. Generic unnamed invented histories replace any real-world example. One coping strategy is recorded for each learner. Source MCQ/choice becomes the two-card route; Aspire is an optional extension. No named exam or organisation wording carried over.

sources.note: Physical row 16 is Spring 1 row 1. Weekly outcome, focus, lesson outcome and evidence verified exactly. Source timing 5/8/10/12/5 retained. Named qualifications and source-only website suggestions omitted; all activity uses prepared in-pack cards. Raw workbook not distributed.
Accepted clean layout and folder shape only. Current content comes from the BUILD Careers scheme row and current owner instruction.

Correct Tuesday P3 line to BUILD Careers. Keep accepted GROW Careers packs unchanged for a separate line; no further GROW Careers until asked. Tuesday 5 January 2027 P3, 40 minutes, up to five learners. Invented stories, generic jobs, visual and choice-based tasks. Current queue is BUILD Careers Weeks 1–6, then LAUNCH Careers Spring 1 Week 1. One per return; pause for Downloaded.

source_end_check: Can the student identify one positive response to career change?
source_sequence_verbatim: Arrival/retrieval linked to previous careers learning → I Do: explain/model careers can change with concrete examples → We Do: guided sorting/annotating/scenario discussion → You Do: Career-story sequencing; discuss change without framing it as failure; students identify one strategy for coping with an unexpected change. → 1:1/whole-class review → exit check and add evidence to Careers Portfolio.
timing: Recall job and career with picture choices.
Pre-teach words, then model A with pictures and concrete examples.
Sort B together, discuss the change, check learning and choose a coping step.
Sequence C through whole-set or step-by-step choices; identify adaptation and one coping strategy.
Private feedback, one next step and reply; add actual evidence to Careers Portfolio.

routes.Supported: Use the pictures, short captions, word bank and A model. Offer two cards at a time or fix the first card. Read, point, sign, type or use an exact scribe. Log any supplied order or answer.
routes.Independent: Use all four C cards with the picture and word bank. Put them in order, identify the learning card and choose one coping step. Usual reading, typing and communication aids remain available.
routes.Aspire: Explain how the new learning helped the person move to a new job. Suggest another useful coping step. More writing or public sharing is not required.

choices.label: Whole set
choices.task: Use all four C cards. Point, place or record their letters in order.

choices.task: Choose the first C card from two options, then the next, until all four are ordered. Record supplied choices.

colour_blind_safe: Pictures are paired with text and card letters. Words and order cues carry meaning; no colour-only codes.

worked_examples_status: All worked examples, people and job histories are invented. Pictures show generic work/support types, not portraits of one person across a story. No real person, employer, provider, place, product or platform is named.
private_help_route: Ask a trusted adult or use the school’s help route. Point to HELP, write a request or ask for a private talk. Pass, pause and a supported return are available. If one adult is busy, seek another through the route. Do not ask for personal job-loss stories or family finances.
typed_and_scribed_routes: Either task route can use Evidence Sheet page 2, Type instead, with blank sequence fields. Use the usual save routine, lesson code and work reference; share privately. A scribe captures exact words/selections, reads back quietly and allows correction. Record usual access separately from an adult-supplied answer.
worked_example_and_fade: After A, privately ask which card shows learning: K or L. Key L. If unsure, read the captions and model change versus response again. Keep pictures, word bank and the full A example. Fade answer cues when secure; do not remove communication or reading access.
adaptations: Cognition and Learning: short captions, four-card sequence, two-choice route and visible model. Communication and Interaction: one instruction, processing time, word bank, sentence frames and usual aid. SEMH: calm predictable stages, pass, supported pause and return; no public questioning. Sensory and Physical: large pictures/text, no colour-only codes, pointing instead of moving cards. EAL: pre-teach words and plan in any language.
misconceptions: A job is one role; a career can include several roles and learning. Change is not failure. A job ending is the change; learning a new skill is one response. Learning again is possible but does not guarantee a job. Pictures show types of work, not portraits that must look identical across the story.

main_hinge.claim: Learning to pack boxes at S is the response to changed shift times at P.

parallel_hinge.claim: Learning a new skill can help with change; a new job does not mean failure.

success: Put a four-event career story in order.
Identify where the person adapted by learning a new skill.
Choose one useful coping strategy for the invented story.

evidence.description: Career-story sequence / resilience note. Keep actual C sequence, change, adaptation, coping step, access, supplied answers, first response, one NS and reply.

assessment: Exact source evidence: Career-story sequence / resilience note. Keep the actual C order, change card, adaptation card or explanation, one coping strategy, access, answer prompts, first response, NS and reply. Secure sequencing is V T W U; secure adaptation identifies W/new learning in response to T/job ending. Log each separately. Partial evidence is retained; a pass is unobserved. A supported sequence is not recorded as independently ordered. Do not infer personal resilience or future employment success.
where_this_leads: This helps me see that work plans can change and that I can ask for help with a next step.

pupil_text: I DO MODEL
Story A Our model
This is a made-up work story. Read it in this order.
K is the change. L shows new learning. They could ask for help.
J  First, a person packs boxes.
K  The job ends.

Students understand that career journeys are not always straight and that people may change jobs or retrain.
I can put a simple career story in order and identify where someone adapted to change.
Source: BUILD Careers, physical row 16 / Spring 1 row 1. Focus F16, weekly outcome E16, lesson outcome G16; sequence H16 and timing I16.

A career can include different jobs and learning. A change does not mean a person has failed. Use invented stories to put events in order, spot a response to change and choose one coping strategy. No claim is made that retraining always leads quickly to a new job.

Put the four story events in order. Identify where the person learned a new skill to adapt. Choose one useful coping step. Record the first two checks separately; the coping note adds the response required by the sequence.

Books, pens, up to five sets of the Support Cards, Vocabulary Mat and staff evidence record. Adult may cut the rows into reusable cards beforehand; pupils do not write on the print references. Use pointing or card letters if loose cards are unsuitable. Confirm a private help route and place for a supported pause. No internet, login or personal phone needed.
This helps me see that work plans can change and that I can ask for help with a next step.
Recall job and career with picture choices.
Pre-teach words, then model A with pictures and concrete examples.
Sort B together, discuss the change, check learning and choose a coping step.
Sequence C through whole-set or step-by-step choices; identify adaptation and one coping strategy.
Private feedback, one next step and reply; add actual evidence to Careers Portfolio.
5 + 8 + 10 + 12 + 5 = 40 minutes, following I16. Processing time and brief pauses are included. Give one instruction at a time. Slides 7 and 8 are alternatives in the same 23–35-minute block.

0–5: choose the picture of packing boxes or tending plants, then recall job as work someone does. If previous learning is missing, supply the definition. 5–9: pre-teach job, career, change and learn again using the pictures and short definitions. 9–13: model A in J K L M order. Point to K as the change and L as adapting through new learning. Model one coping step: ask for help. Read the exact outcome, then explain it simply.

13–19: use B in the printed mixed order P Q R S. Offer two cards for what comes first, then build R P S Q. Ask privately what changed and what the person learned. Read the captions; pictures support meaning but do not prove the order. 19–23: hinge and short scenario discussion. A changed work time is not failure. Each learner chooses or states one useful coping step; no personal example is needed.

23–35: offer C as a whole set or two cards at a time. For supported choices use V/U for first, then T/W for next, then W/U. Keep A as the model without giving C’s answer. Learners point, place or record letters in a book, type or use an aid/scribe. Identify adaptation and give one coping strategy. Log all supplied choices and prompts.

35–38: check sequence and adaptation privately, set one NS and retain the reply. 38–40: each learner gives a coping step or corrects “changing jobs means failure”. Add actual sequence/resilience note to Careers Portfolio. No public retelling or family employment discussion.
Use the pictures, short captions, word bank and A model. Offer two cards at a time or fix the first card. Read, point, sign, type or use an exact scribe. Log any supplied order or answer.
Use all four C cards with the picture and word bank. Put them in order, identify the learning card and choose one coping step. Usual reading, typing and communication aids remain available.
Explain how the new learning helped the person move to a new job. Suggest another useful coping step. More writing or public sharing is not required.

After A, privately ask which card shows learning: K or L. Key L. If unsure, read the captions and model change versus response again. Keep pictures, word bank and the full A example. Fade answer cues when secure; do not remove communication or reading access.

Main B: which card shows adapting? A the shift times change (P); B they learn to pack boxes (S). Key B. If unclear, point to learn in A and B, then use the parallel check. Parallel A: A learning a new skill can help with change; B a new job means failure. Key A. A pass is unobserved. Recheck privately before the individual task.

Cognition and Learning: short captions, four-card sequence, two-choice route and visible model. Communication and Interaction: one instruction, processing time, word bank, sentence frames and usual aid. SEMH: calm predictable stages, pass, supported pause and return; no public questioning. Sensory and Physical: large pictures/text, no colour-only codes, pointing instead of moving cards. EAL: pre-teach words and plan in any language.

Prompt ladder: 1 point to place/instruction; 2 ask a short question; 3 rephrase; 4 provide scaffold/choice; 5 model the first step only, then return the task. In input, point to job and learning pictures; in guided work, prompt an event clue; in individual work, log actual help without supplying the sequence.

Ask a trusted adult or use the school’s help route. Point to HELP, write a request or ask for a private talk. Pass, pause and a supported return are available. If one adult is busy, seek another through the route. Do not ask for personal job-loss stories or family finances.

Either task route can use Evidence Sheet page 2, Type instead, with blank sequence fields. Use the usual save routine, lesson code and work reference; share privately. A scribe captures exact words/selections, reads back quietly and allows correction. Record usual access separately from an adult-supplied answer.

Exact source evidence: Career-story sequence / resilience note. Keep the actual C order, change card, adaptation card or explanation, one coping strategy, access, answer prompts, first response, NS and reply. Secure sequencing is V T W U; secure adaptation identifies W/new learning in response to T/job ending. Log each separately. Partial evidence is retained; a pass is unobserved. A supported sequence is not recorded as independently ordered. Do not infer personal resilience or future employment success.

A job is one role; a career can include several roles and learning. Change is not failure. A job ending is the change; learning a new skill is one response. Learning again is possible but does not guarantee a job. Pictures show types of work, not portraits that must look identical across the story.

Give one NS such as move the change before the learning, or point to the new skill. VF verbal feedback; WS worked with support; I independent; // self-edit; ? read back; E actual banked evidence. R only after Voice, Audience, NS and response in the same colour, on the same page or usual mode. Offer to the Communication portfolio. Staff confirm any accredited mapping.

All people, jobs, event sequences and quoted history are invented. Pictures are generic work/support symbols, not real people or places and not a visual record of one person. No real employer, provider, product or platform is named. No claims about entry rules, wages or guaranteed routes. The lesson needs no live research. If a concern arises, listen calmly, avoid probing or secrecy promises and follow usual procedures; keep concerns outside shared work.

I can put a simple career story in order and identify where someone adapted to change.

A job is one work role; a career may include several roles and learning. Jobs and work times may change. Retraining is learning skills for a different kind of work. The examples are invented histories, not claims about typical routes, entry requirements or likely hiring. Do not equate a change with failure or blame.

Accept the matching picture of packing boxes or tending plants. Supply definitions if earlier Careers teaching is missing. Pre-teach job, career, change and learn again, then connect learn again to retrain. Read one caption at a time. Visuals are generic symbols, not portraits of the same person.

J K L M. J packs boxes; K job ends; L learns plant care; M tends plants in a new job. K is the unexpected change; L is adapting through new learning. One coping strategy is asking for help with a next step. Private model check K/L: key L for new learning.

R P S Q. R serves food; P shift times change; S learns to pack boxes; Q packs boxes in a new job. P is the change; S is adapting. Ask for help or make a small plan are valid coping strategies. Accept other safe, relevant support steps.

Main key B: learning to pack boxes at S is the response to change. The changed shifts at P are the event. Parallel key A: learning a new skill can help with change. If unclear, reread the captions and contrast event with response privately. A pass is unobserved.

V T W U. V tends plants; T job ends; W learns to mend bikes; U mends bikes in a new job. Adaptation is W/new learning in response to the ending at T. A learner may point to the correct card or give equivalent words. The task is ordering a story, not copying a paragraph.

Whole set: give the printed mixed T U V W set. Two at a time: offer V/U for first; T/W for next; W/U for then; place the final U. Read captions neutrally. If the first card is fixed, record that help. Both routes meet the same goal; independence records must reflect the support actually supplied.

Each learner chooses or says one strategy for the unexpected change. Accept ask someone for help, make a small plan, or agree a pause then plan a step. Give a reason if ready. These are helpful possibilities, not guarantees. No personal example is required.

Link new learning to the next job and offer another support step. The story does not show all real-world barriers or assure a quick job change. Do not invent wages, qualifications, training lengths or actual employers.

One NS may be to put the job ending before the new learning, or to identify the skill learned. Retain the first sequence and the reply. Exit can give a coping strategy or correct “changing jobs means failure”. Change may happen for many reasons; the person’s worth is not judged.

Exact evidence: Career-story sequence / resilience note. Record order and adaptation separately, with one coping strategy. Secure order V T W U; secure adaptation W/new learning. Preserve partial evidence. No response, including a pass, is unobserved. Record fixed cards, two-choice prompts, adult models and supplied answers apart from normal reading, communication or scribing access.

Evidence Sheet page 2 has blank editable fields. Either choice can be typed. Save through the usual routine with lesson code and work reference, and share privately. Scribe exact words or selections, read back and allow correction. A book or aid is valid. No online system is needed.

R follows Voice, Audience, one NS and the learner’s reply. E means actual evidence banked. Add the sequence and resilience note to Careers Portfolio. Offer to the Communication portfolio. Staff confirm any accredited mapping from actual work.

Trusted adult or the school’s help route. Point to HELP, write or ask for a private talk. Pass, supported pause and return are available. Do not ask for real family work histories, job losses or finances. Listen calmly if a concern arises, avoid probing or secrecy promises and follow normal procedures. Keep concerns out of public evidence.
